searches.purpose: Locate independent history, Axline's foundational record, method and variant boundaries, evidence syntheses, trauma-specific outcomes, professional safety guidance, Indigenous cultural critique and contemporary institutional continuation while excluding ordinary play, educational play, hospital therapeutic play, filial therapy, Theraplay, sandplay and generic play-based interventions unless the source explicitly identifies their relationship to professional psychotherapy

items.title: Play Therapy: History, Theories, and Research
items.rights_note: Sacred Heart institutional record and abstract for Hudspeth's encyclopedia chapter on history, research and the directive-to-nondirective continuum; the publisher chapter body is not cached or treated as read.

items.title: Play Therapy: The Inner Dynamics of Childhood
items.rights_note: Open Library record for Axline's 1947 nondirective play-therapy text; the copyrighted body is not cached or treated as read, and Axline's approach is an ancestor of child-centered play therapy rather than a synonym for every directive or integrative play therapy.

items.title: Play Therapy: Considerations and Applications for the Practitioner
items.rights_note: Open clinical overview describes play as developmentally adapted communication and distinguishes child-centered, psychoanalytic, Jungian, Gestalt and other variants; an overview of diverse practice models is not evidence that their mechanisms or outcomes are equivalent.

items.title: Systematic Review of Common and Specific Factors in Play Therapy for Young People With Intellectual Disability
items.rights_note: Open systematic review examines common and specific factors in work with young people with intellectual disability and warns that prior reviews sometimes combine child-centered and filial approaches; findings cannot be generalized to all children or all play-therapy models.

items.title: A Meta-Analytic Review of Child-Centered Play Therapy Approaches
items.rights_note: Publicly readable copy of a meta-analysis of 52 controlled CCPT studies; the moderate pooled estimate and moderators apply to child-centered approaches in the included designs, not to all therapies involving play, and funding by the Center for Play Therapy is recorded as context.

items.title: Child-Centered Play Therapy for Youths Who Have Experienced Trauma: A Systematic Literature Review
items.rights_note: Open review found only seven quantitative CCPT outcome articles for trauma-exposed youth, with some consistency for selected outcomes but important design limitations; this does not establish equivalence with trauma-focused CBT or efficacy for PTSD generally.

items.title: Ethical Framework Principles
items.rights_note: Play Therapy International framework places the child's interests first and addresses autonomy, beneficence, non-maleficence, justice, fidelity and self-respect amid competing obligations; it is professional ethical guidance rather than an adverse-event review or local legal standard.
items.failure_note: The Association for Play Therapy best-practices PDF returned HTTP 403; the publicly readable Play Therapy International ethical framework was selected without bypassing access controls.

items.title: Cultural Considerations in Play Therapy With Aboriginal Children in Canada
items.rights_note: Open First Peoples journal article foregrounds colonial harm, family and community context and the lack of adequate culturally competent practice guidance; it offers considerations rather than evidence that one adaptation represents First Nations, Métis and Inuit peoples collectively.

items.title: Center for Play Therapy
items.rights_note: Official University of North Texas center page documents current research, training, databases and child-centered play-therapy programmes; one university center's continuation does not define worldwide practice or validate every play-therapy school.
items.failure_note: The Association for Play Therapy About page returned HTTP 403; the University of North Texas Center for Play Therapy was selected as a readable current institutional source.
